g.text: TLS 1.3 handshake, and what mTLS adds
proves it owns the private key
Asymmetric crypto is used only to agree on a key.
Everything after that is symmetric, because it's
In mTLS the server also asks the CLIENT for a
certificate, and verifies it the same way.
Both sides prove who they are.
TLS 1.2 needed 2 round trips. 1.3 folds key agreement into the first
flight, so it's 1 — and drops the weak ciphers that made 1.2 dangerous.
